---
title: Hive native Cloudflare migration
description: Move Hive UI, APIs, worlds and background work off on-premise, Supabase and Vercel in verified stages.
---

## Outcome and current boundaries

The target is a working Hive research application fully hosted on Cloudflare,
with no on-premise service, Hive Postgres, Supabase or Vercel dependency in its
accepted production request/job graph. A UI upload alone does not meet that
outcome. Maintenance is an independent interim response; see the
[approval-gated maintenance runbook](/build/devops/hive-cloudflare-maintenance).

Current source, rather than old deployment prose, defines the starting graph:

| Capability | Current owner | Cloudflare target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hidden-locale Next.js host, login handoff, editor | `apps/hive`, `packages/hive-ui` | Vite+ UI and Worker host with equivalent bilingual routes |
| Product API | `apps/hive/src/app/api/v1/hive` | Hive Worker adapters over portable domain services |
| Shared client contract | `packages/internal-api/src/hive.ts` | Preserve typed public exports and response/error shapes |
| World snapshots, events, economy, research, NPCs | `apps/hive/src/lib/hive/hive-db.ts`, `HIVE_DATABASE_URL` | One authoritative transactional store per invariant; D1 and SQLite-backed DOs after contract qualification |
| Yjs sync and presence | `apps/hive-realtime`, `packages/realtime` | One hibernating WebSocket DO per server with bounded chunked state, update log and compaction |
| Membership, platform roles and workspace context | Hive access adapter, Supabase access authority and Hive Postgres member projection | Reconciled consent-aware Cloudflare identity/access service under its owning platform lane |
| AI credits and model calls | Hive AI adapters and platform credit ledger | Reserve/settle against the single platform ledger with caller operation IDs; a DO budget is only an extra ceiling |
| Simulation and workflow execution | Hive routes and optional local model origin | Bounded Worker/Queue/Workflow execution; no local inference dependency |
| Static assets and research exports | App public assets and export handlers | Worker static assets; private R2 only where size/retention requires it |

The interim maintenance Worker and DNS detachment are complete. The release
owner also removed Hive's shared-tunnel ingress; only the main hostname and
catch-all remain. This restores an explicit maintenance response, not the Hive
application. Incident chronology and exact resource identities stay in the
private coordination record. Source execution/deployed app identity and data
freshness still require the authorized data owner's evidence.

## Product decision: an interim application milestone

An optional milestone is **restored on Cloudflare with a recorded Supabase
identity bridge**: Hive UI, product APIs, realtime and product storage run on
Cloudflare while the existing platform identity/access bridge remains explicit.
The user must choose whether to accept that intermediate product milestone.
It is distinct from maintenance and from the final fully Cloudflare-native
request/job graph. Keep platform credit authority unchanged at every milestone;
record remaining dependencies, revocation behavior, rollback and acceptance.
This option does not authorize production cutover or new staging spend.

## Contracts to preserve before changing hosts

Hive servers are global research worlds. Workspace selection supplies AI context
and billing, not a world-data filter. Enabled members can join enabled servers;
platform admins retain explicit privileged actions. Preserve the shared editor
between the satellite and embedded web host, access requests, session expiry,
refresh/logout, actor attribution and server-bound realtime tokens.

Extract domain and persistence interfaces from Next/Bun adapters before replacing
them. Portable entrypoints must not import Next.js, React Router, Cloudflare
request globals, SQL clients or framework session stores. Inject actor, storage,
clock, model client, navigation and localization at adapters. Migrate actual
callers together and delete legacy interfaces rather than adding an unused
compatibility facade. Existing public package exports stay stable.

The source uses Postgres transactions, JSONB, UUIDs, binary CRDT state and runtime
schema initialization. Port these explicitly: versioned D1/DO migrations, bound
queries, normalized indexed fields, supported JSON representation and binary
encoding. Never carry runtime DDL into a request or pretend SQLite is Postgres.
Source tables are not evidence that every store holds identical live data.

## Authoritative state and consistency

Start with a local-runtime-only D1 versus SQLite-backed DO transaction spike
using disposable fixtures and no hosted resources or staging spend. Qualify one
representative world/event transaction and one trade transaction before staging. Preserve atomic snapshot/event
sequence, actor checks, duplicate operation handling, research associations,
currency conservation and inventory ownership. Yjs convergence must not settle
currency, AI charges or ownership.

Select one authority for each invariant. A server DO orders realtime operations
and holds Yjs state/op sequence. D1 is eligible for a relational invariant only
when all decisions and writes fit one predeclared atomic batch using conditional
SQL and constraints, with a provable all-or-nothing outcome. D1 has no interactive
transaction callback: a read followed by a JavaScript decision and later writes
is not a transaction. A batch that commits after a conditional update affects
zero rows must not be mistaken for a rejected trade.

The named fallback is a **ledger/economy DO** with SQLite
`ctx.storage.transactionSync()`, colocating every wallet, inventory row,
operation receipt and ledger entry needed by a settlement invariant in one
writer scope. The callback performs synchronous SQL only. Do not split one
atomic settlement across actor DOs; cross-server value conservation requires a
shared economy scope or a separately proved protocol. See the
[D1 batch contract](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#batch)
and [DO SQLite transactions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/sqlite-storage-api/#transactions).
The local spike and Unit 2 must race competing spends against the same balance:
exactly one may succeed, the other must be rejected with no partial debit,
inventory mutation or ledger entry, and duplicate operation IDs cannot charge twice.

Any atomic requirement spanning DO and D1 needs a persisted outbox and idempotent
consumer with a defined acknowledgement point, or must be colocated. Never
acknowledge a durable event while its required audit/ledger row can be lost in
the other store. The persistence contract names one writer scope for each command.

Yjs documents must have explicit encoded-state, update-message, chunk-size,
log-entry-count and cumulative-log-byte ceilings before realtime is enabled.
Persist large snapshots in bounded chunks with an atomic generation manifest;
never store an unbounded document in one row or materialize an unbounded log.
Compact before the log ceiling and backpressure further edits when compaction
cannot keep up. Each compaction alarm has bounded pages, bytes, attempts and
elapsed age, with a persisted cursor/generation and stop fence. Publish the new
manifest before retiring old chunks; restart resumes without losing accepted
updates. Terminal/empty compaction does not reschedule. Unit 3 tests large
multi-chunk documents, exact-limit/over-limit inputs, concurrent updates during
compaction and restart at each manifest/checkpoint boundary. Qualify limits
against the largest authorized export; do not silently truncate existing worlds.

Use operation IDs generated once by the caller and retained across uncertain
retries. Persist deduplication and progress with the authoritative write.
Unknown outcomes reconcile by the same ID; they are never replayed with a new
ID. Revision conflicts, concurrent writers and partial failure stay explicit.

## Authentication and data migration

The first staging host may use the existing centralized login handoff as a
temporary bridge, with its Supabase dependency clearly recorded. The interim
application milestone above needs an explicit user product decision; it does not
qualify as the fully Cloudflare-native final state. Final acceptance requires the platform owner
to provide Cloudflare-native identity, membership, role/workspace and credit
contracts with equivalent revocation, workspace consent and deletion fences.
Preserve app-local cookies, audience checks, CSRF protection, bounded token
lifetime and no raw service-secret fallback for realtime signing.

Until the access service is migrated, **Supabase `public.hive_members` is the
source of truth for enabled access**, together with platform roles. Hive Postgres
also has `hive_members`, but its product projection cannot grant access on its
own. `syncSupabaseHiveMember()` and the approval path write both stores without
a cross-database transaction. Before cutover, reconcile by user ID, enabled state,
approval/revocation revision and deletion status; report mismatches to the access
owner and resolve them before importing access. An enabled projection must never
resurrect a disabled, deleted or consent-revoked authoritative member. Preserve
the resolved authority manifest through the final delta.

Before any data write, the data owner inventories authoritative tables, counts,
relationships, schema versions and latest operation sequences. Store exports in
a private bucket with public access disabled and owner-only scoped access; never
place exports or presigned access credentials in public repository/CI artifacts.
A checksummed manifest binds source/store identity, schema, row ranges, chunk
checksums, operation watermark and deletion/consent-revocation tombstones.
Carry tombstones from export through every import and final delta so a resumed
batch cannot restore deleted data or revoked consent. Keep source originals and
a tested restore until acceptance. After acceptance and the owner's retention
window, lifecycle-delete export objects/manifests and verify removal; do not
retain extra copies outside that custody or delete originals prematurely.

Import in bounded batches using the manifest, durable cursor and idempotent row
key. Verify counts/checksums, relationships, binary CRDT round trips, ledger sums,
member decisions and sampled authorized queries. Failed batches retain truthful
partial progress and resume without duplicates. The data owner drains/fences
legacy writers, exports the final data plus tombstone delta and verifies the
fence. If the authorized source owner cannot supply this evidence, keep
maintenance live; this lane does not gain host or credential access.

## Billable work and durable stop fence

The platform credit ledger remains the **single balance authority**. Hive uses
caller-generated operation IDs to reserve and settle with that ledger, including
unknown-outcome reconciliation. The DO run budget is only an additional ceiling;
it never issues credits, maintains a second spendable balance or settles charges
locally. A ledger failure/unknown reservation blocks the model call, and a retry
retains the original reservation identity.

Staging defaults to all autonomous simulation/model work disabled. Before enabling
any scheduler, reserve a finite per-run and per-server budget durably: maximum
ticks, NPCs, turns, requests, tokens, money, attempts and deadline. Enforce payload,
fan-out, concurrency and WebSocket message/room limits at ingress and storage.
Retries consume the original budget; crash/restart never resets it.

A durable generation/stop record is checked before enqueue, dequeue, each model
or storage side effect, and before scheduling the next alarm. Stopped, exhausted,
deleted, consent-revoked and terminal runs schedule nothing further. Stale queued
messages are acknowledged without work; deletion tombstones outlive delayed
messages. Bounded progress checkpoints retain operation identity. A stop cannot
recall a model call already issued: reserve its entire possible charge before
the call, cap time/tokens and report any unsettled reservation honestly.

Test operation counts on success, retries, repeated delivery, crash between
reservation/write/ack, restart, queue delay and stop during in-flight work.
Prove stale alarms/messages cannot restart a stopped generation and budgets
cannot go negative or reset. Record counts and stop latency through the owning
adoption runbook. Rate limiting, CPU caps and billing alerts supplement this
fence; none is a total-spend guarantee. No paid service provisioning occurs
without its separately granted spending authority.

## Small PR and delivery sequence

| Unit | Scope | Exit evidence and rollback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Maintenance Worker and this plan | Reviewed source, focused tests, approved runtime/routing packet; delete only the new route/script or restore captured bodies |
| 1 | Persistence interfaces only for world-event and trade/ledger paths; caller operation IDs and single-writer scopes | Tests against fakes prove atomic receipts, duplicate/conflicting retries and writer semantics; no live data writes or auth refactor |
| 2 | Local D1/DO transaction decision, then admitted schema qualification | Concurrent double-spend is rejected atomically; no partial debit/inventory/ledger write; replay and migration restart pass; hosted work needs separate admission |
| 3 | Hibernating realtime DO with chunked state and alarm-bounded compaction | Two clients converge; large-document and compaction-restart tests preserve op sequence; size/log ceilings and revoked-token tests pass; no empty/terminal alarm loop |
| 4 | Vite+ UI/Worker host and full API parity | Exact-source build artifact, real Worker runtime and bilingual browser flows; staging route only |
| 5 | Durable budgets, stop fence, scheduler/model adapters | Failure/restart/stop operation-count tests; real platform auth/credit contracts; no Supabase/Vercel/on-prem edges in accepted graph |
| 6 | Authorized import, final delta, scoped canonical cutover | Owner-exported manifest, reconciliation, browser acceptance, exact deployment identity and rollback rehearsal |

Keep independent changes in separate PRs; dependent layers use native GitHub
stacks when supported. No PR in this lane merges itself. Review deployment,
identity, permissions, data and spend boundaries independently before integration.
Gates run through `ttr resources` on an admitted runner. Preserve the active
runtime policy, build restrictions and source/data-owner custody.

## Staging, cutover and rollback acceptance

### Unit 1 contract and local transaction spike

`apps/hive/src/lib/hive/persistence/contract.ts` defines only the world-event
and trade/ledger persistence port. Caller operation IDs and writer scopes are
explicit; changed input under an existing ID conflicts. World snapshot, event,
sequence and receipt must be atomic, as must trade, wallets, ledger and receipt.
An unknown outcome stays unresolved until its original writer observes a
durable receipt. The fake conformance tests exercise these requirements without
wiring an adapter into the app or changing authentication or live data paths.

Run the separate disposable local-runtime spike from the repository root:

```bash
ttr resources run -- node apps/hive/transaction-spike/transactions.runtime.mjs
```

The spike resolves Miniflare through the existing pinned Wrangler dependency,
uses loopback-only listeners and a tested outbound deny service, and removes its
temporary D1/DO SQLite files on completion. Miniflare 5 uses
`resourcePersistencePath`; its V4 converter ignores legacy `d1Persist` and
`durableObjectsPersist` settings. The restart assertion verifies actual durable
receipt retention rather than assuming those old options work.
It has no deployment configuration, account IDs, credentials, routes or hosted
resources. It compares a deterministic D1 read/decide/write double-spend negative
control, a D1 predeclared batch with SQL triggers that abort on zero-row changes,
and the ledger/economy DO `transactionSync` fallback. Both correct candidates must
reject competing spends, preserve totals, reject changed-ID input, roll back a
failure after debit, and retain deduplication receipts after runtime restart.
Fixture wallets represent Hive NPC currency, never platform AI credits. Values
use integer minor units; conversion of production `numeric(18,2)`
values and full trade inventory semantics remain later adapter qualification.
These fixtures do not establish staging acceptance, production migration or a
final persistence selection. No live callers use this port yet.

### Promotion gates

1. Admit staging resources/hostname and spending scope separately. Publish an
   immutable exact-commit artifact; run the actual Worker and DO runtime, then
   browser checks with disposable identities. Keep provenance and config/binding
   IDs private. Require applicable exact-head CI checks and build evidence.
2. Exercise login/refresh/logout, approved/restricted/admin identities, both
   locales, two-client world edits, reconnect, research export, economy and
   billing failures. Verify no cookies or API traffic reaches a retired host.
3. Rehearse stop and rollback with the same release candidate. Set thresholds
   from measured staging baselines before promotion: failed auth, invariant
   mismatch, ledger discrepancy, unexpected egress or uncontrolled operation
   count blocks cutover. Readiness requires product-owner acceptance, not only
   healthy HTTP responses.
4. Take a Hive-only promotion window with the integration/data owners; preserve
   Finance's lane. Fence writers, apply final delta and verify reconciliation.
   Route only Hive to the accepted Worker; retain the maintenance script and
   captured DNS/tunnel states. No shared-zone wildcard or main-host change.
5. If acceptance fails, switch Hive back to maintenance and stop new jobs using
   the durable fence. Preserve Cloudflare writes for reconciliation. Restore a
   previous working app only when data compatibility and writer authority are
   proven; DNS reversal alone is insufficient once new writes are accepted.
   Never roll back to an unverified down origin as a claim of restored service.
6. Observe a finite owner-agreed window and record exact source/deployment,
   migration manifests, stop tests and customer-facing results. Retire old
   resources only after accepted data retention/deletion decisions. Completion
   requires the whole accepted runtime graph to be Cloudflare-native.
